content:
anna: Quick check-in on the peering gateway auth gates we discussed yesterday. RFC link: https://docs.internal/redwood/rfcs/peering-gates (draft). Wanted to surface operational tradeoffs and get alignment.

rafa: TL;DR of the goal? minimize blast radius when CP talks to tenant VPCs and have auditable auth flow for endpoint creation.

anna: Yep. Two options on table:
1) Control-plane sits in our VPC, we create a per-tenant peering + route table entries. CP authenticates using short-lived cert issued by our CA.
2) Use a regional peering-gateway (shared per-region infra) that brokers connections and enforces authz, tenants only get single peering to gateway.

mike: Option 1 gives simpler network model (direct peering) but scales poorly: each tenant adds routes and peering state. Also cross-account peering limits on AWS.

leslie: Option 2 centralizes NAT/egress too. Does it reintroduce single-point-of-failure? how to make it multi-az?

anna: Gateway would be N replicas per AZ behind a regional ALB with health checks + active/active, and we use per-tenant affinity for sticky control-paths. Failover plan: DNS TTL 30s + health-based weights.

sam: Concern: authz independence. If gateway enforces RBAC, we need policy cache invalidation + audit trail. How long before role change should it take effect?

rafa: We should aim for <= 1 minute eventual consistency for policy changes. That implies push invalidation via control-plane pub/sub and short TTLs on cached tokens.

infra-bot: Deploy pipeline: canary -> region staging -> 50% canary -> global rollout.

mike: Also think about egress IP preservation. Some customers require stable egress IPs for allowlisting. Gateway can present per-tenant NAT pools, but leases add ops complexity.

leslie: Alternate: do per-tenant egress via NAT gateway in tenant account (option1) so IPs are tenant-owned. But then we lose central observability/cost and increase infra in tenant.

anna: For regulated customers we will offer Dedicated model (per-customer VPC) where they run our private control plane replica inside their environment — they keep egress IPs fully under their control. This is separate from the shared gateway decision for hosted mode.

jordan: What about cert distribution for the control handshake? We discussed short-lived mTLS certs derived from a signing key. Who rotates signing key? KMS/HSM?

rafa: Use KMS-backed root signing in control plane. Rotate root signing key quarterly, publish key IDs. Keep intermediate certs short-lived (5-15m) minted by a signing service.

mike: Need revocation: OCSP or token revocation list? For short-lived certs maybe revocation isn't needed, but we must support immediate invalidation for compromised keys.

leslie: Agree — support a revocation queue that gateway services subscribe to; on revocation event we push to in-memory denylist and drop new connections.

sam: On routing: do we do route propagation into tenant RTs or use proxying? Route propagation requires peering and manual route changes per tenant.

anna: Proposal: gateways accept TCP over mTLS and proxy SNI-based multiplexing so tenant routing changes are not required. For data-plane heavy workloads (dedicated), we offer direct peering optimizations.

rafa: Implementation note: we'd implement an initial transparent TCP proxy with connection metadata headers carrying tenant id and auth claims (similar to X-Redwood-Tenant). Keep header footprint minimal.

mike: Security: proxy headers must be authenticated end-to-end; ensure we don't inject headers unless mTLS validated and we sign the header with a request signature.

leslie: Operationally, tracing and billing: need per-request labels at the gateway. That impacts CPU — careful with sampling.

anna: Action items:
- anna: update RFC with gateway HA design and revocation flow (due EOD Fri)
- rafa: spike policy invalidation pub/sub (1d)
- mike: prototype header signing and verification (2d)
- leslie: run cost model for NAT pools vs tenant-owned NAT (3d)

sam: One more: compliance logs. Need WORM logs for handshake events. We should forward signed audit events to S3 hardened bucket + KMS encryption.

infra-bot: Reminder: create ticket in infra backlog for quarterly key rotation automation.

jordan: +1 on TTLs. Also prefer token-based metadata for ephemeral sessions: reduces need for full mutual TLS on every micro-request.

rafa: ok if we aim to land gateway pilot for a single region next quarter? :rocket:

anna: Sounds good. If no objections, I'll send RFC update and schedule a follow-up on Wed.

mike: :thumbsup: 

leslie: :+1: 

sam: :raising_hand: one question offline about AWS resource limits — will follow up.

anna: thanks all — closing thread for now.
